newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai soybeans end mostly up on short-covering.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai soybeans end mostly up on short-covering.

text.p: Shanghai soybean futures ended mostly up on Thursday on short-covering by retail investors, traders said.
The most active September contract ended at an intraday low of 3,315 yuan ($399) per tonne, unchanged from Wednesday's close. It opened at a high of 3,320.
March rose 25 to 3,130 yuan per tonne, May 70 to 3,170, July seven to 3,253, November four to 3,330 and the January 1998 contract four to 3,340.
Combined volume rose to 22,400 tonnes from 19,100.
Traders said retail investors dominated Thursday trading with most investors staying on the sidelines because of an ongoing lack of market-moving news.
"Short-covering from retail investors was the major factor behind today's rises," one trader said.
"But many investors were not very interested in soybean contracts because there's nothing moving the market," he added.
Analysts said they expected soybeans to move around current levels over the next few days.
